title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: Grilled chicken tikka in a creamy tomato and spice sauce
excerpt: Britain's adopted national dish: chargrilled chicken tikka pieces in a richly spiced, cream-enriched tomato sauce. A British-Indian creation that has become one of the most eaten dishes in the country.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is widely claimed to be Britain's most popular dish, and its origins are contested. The most commonly cited story credits Ali Ahmed Aslam of the Shish Mahal restaurant in Glasgow with its creation in the 1970s, when a customer complained that the chicken tikka was too dry and asked for a sauce; Aslam reportedly added condensed tomato soup, cream, and spices to create the dish. However, the dish also has strong parallels with murgh makhani (butter chicken) and Indian cooking traditions, suggesting it may have evolved simultaneously across British Indian restaurants. What is clear is that tikka masala is a British-Indian creation rather than a traditional Indian dish. It differs from butter chicken in its use of marinated and grilled chicken tikka as the starting point and its slightly more assertive spicing.

content.text: The tikka marinade needs at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. The colour of the sauce comes from the tomato and the spices; resist adding food colouring. The sauce should be blended until very smooth after the initial tomato cook; this creates the restaurant-style velvety consistency.

items.preparation: for the marinade; gives the red colour

content.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, 1 teaspoon of the garam masala, the smoked paprika, and half the cumin. Season and marinate for at least 4 hours. Thread onto skewers and grill or cook in a very hot pan until charred in spots and cooked through.

Melt the butter in a large pan. Cook the onion for 12 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger, remaining spices, and tomato puree. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes. Blend until very smooth.

Return the sauce to the pan. Add the cream and the grilled chicken. Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the chicken is heated through and the sauce has thickened. Taste and season. Serve with basmati rice or naan, scattered with fresh coriander.
